issues.body: `migration_owned` still represents provenance as a set of bd-ids and requires exactly one marker-bearing issue for an id. If a legitimate pre-label issue satisfies the migration title and write-author contract, an unprivileged attacker can add a second issue with the same marker. `migration_owned` then omits the id, and `_marker_index` authenticates neither issue, producing `missing_issues` and a failed `--verify`. The added decoy-beside-real test does not cover this path because `full` gives the legitimate issue `MIGRATION_LABEL`, independently authenticating it.
issues.fix_hint: Represent migration-owned provenance at issue granularity, for example authenticated `(bd-id, issue-number)` pairs, and make `_marker_index` authenticate only that exact legacy issue. Add a focused test with an unlabeled, non-checkpointed issue having valid migration title/write-author provenance plus an unprivileged duplicate marker; verification must remain clean and report only the duplicate under `unauthenticated_markers`.
issues.title: A decoy still invalidates legitimate pre-label migration-owned provenance

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant: the round-4 provenance-granularity defect remains. `migration_owned` still returns bd-id strings only and rejects an id when any second marker-bearing issue exists, while `_marker_index` authenticates legacy issues using `bid in owned`. Thus an unprivileged duplicate marker suppresses the legitimate pre-label issue's migration-owned authentication and makes verification fail with a missing issue. The tests still authenticate the real issue through `MIGRATION_LABEL`, or test `migration_owned` separately; none exercises an unlabeled, non-checkpointed legitimate migration-owned issue alongside a decoy.
